/-!
# Regions of the memory, and the cells that a step leaves alone

A region is given by its first address `a` and its number `n` of cells.  `Inside a n b` says that
the cell `b` lies in it, `Outside a n b` that it does not, and `Apart a n a' n'` that two regions do
not meet.  `InOrder top [(a, n), (a', n'), …]` says that the listed regions lie one behind the other
and end at or below `top`.  All of these abbreviate linear inequalities.

`SameOn K μ μ'` says that the memory `μ'` agrees with `μ` on every cell that satisfies `K`.  It is
the one notion of "these cells are unchanged": a routine promises `SameOn K μ μ'` for the cells
`K` that it leaves alone.  (It is `Set.EqOn μ' μ {b | K b}`, stated with a predicate: the conditions
`K b` that occur are linear inequalities between addresses and are used as such.)  The usual choices
of `K` have names.

* `SameOutside μ μ' a n`: all cells outside one region; `SameOutside2` and `SameOutside3`: all cells
  outside two or three regions.
* `Kept μ μ' fr`: all cells below the free pointer `fr`.
* `KeptBut μ μ' fr out len`: all cells below `fr` outside the region of an output.

## How a fact is carried from one memory to a later one

A predicate `X` about a memory has one lemma of the name `X.keep` and of the form

  `theorem X.keep (h : X μ …) (hs : SameOn K μ μ' := by light_keep) : X μ' …`

where `K` describes the cells that `X` reads; `Seg.keep` is the model.  The argument `hs` has a
default proof.  So `h.keep`, with no argument, stands for "`h` still holds in the memory that is
asked for here".  The default proof `light_keep` uses every hypothesis of the form `SameOn _ ν ν'`
in the context, that is, the promises of the steps that were taken since `h` was obtained, and the
inequalities in the context that say where the regions lie.  In the proofs a promise is named when
the step is taken, as `same₂` in `rintro _ μ₂ ⟨sY, same₂⟩`.

`wrote μ dst f j` is the memory `μ` after a loop has written `f 0`, …, `f (j - 1)` to the cells from
`dst`.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Light
open _root_.Light


/-! ## Regions -/









/-! ## Memories that agree on some cells -/

/-- The memory `μ'` agrees with `μ` on every cell that satisfies `K`. -/
def SameOn (K : ℕ → Prop) (μ μ' : ℕ → ℤ) : Prop := ∀ b, K b → μ' b = μ b

/-- The memory `μ'` agrees with `μ` outside the `n` cells from address `a`. -/
abbrev SameOutside (μ μ' : ℕ → ℤ) (a n : ℕ) : Prop := _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.SameOn (_root_.Light.Outside a n) μ μ'

/-- The memory `μ'` agrees with `μ` outside the `n` cells from `a` and the `m` cells from `b`. -/
abbrev SameOutside2 (μ μ' : ℕ → ℤ) (a n b m : ℕ) : Prop :=
  _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.SameOn (fun x => _root_.Light.Outside a n x ∧ _root_.Light.Outside b m x) μ μ'



/-- No cell below the free pointer has changed. -/
abbrev Kept (μ μ' : ℕ → ℤ) (fr : ℕ) : Prop := _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.SameOn (· < fr) μ μ'

/-- No cell below the free pointer has changed, except the `len` cells from `out`. -/
abbrev KeptBut (μ μ' : ℕ → ℤ) (fr out len : ℕ) : Prop :=
  _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.SameOn (fun x => x < fr ∧ _root_.Light.Outside out len x) μ μ'

variable {K K' K₁ K₂ : ℕ → Prop} {μ μ' μ'' : ℕ → ℤ} {b : ℕ}

/-!
# The light language

A small imperative language with procedures and recursion, in which the paper's procedures can be
written almost as printed.  It is a proof device: a program of this language is compiled
(`compileProgram`) to the word RAM of the end statement, and the compiler is proved to keep results
and, up to a constant factor that depends on the program text only, step counts.

* A program is a finite piece of data: a list of procedure bodies.  It contains no Lean functions.
* The memory is an array of integers addressed by natural numbers.  Each running procedure has local
  variables 0, 1, 2, ….
* Arithmetic: +, −, ×.  There is no division.  Comparisons (<, =) occur as the tests of if and
  while.
* Every executed operation costs one step: each constant, variable, operation and load of an
  expression, each comparison, assignment, store, branch, call and return.
* A run is subject to limits: it forms no value of absolute value above `word`, touches no cell at
  an address ≥ `space`, and nests calls at most `depth` deep.  A run that would break a limit does
  not exist.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Light
open _root_.Light






/-- Expressions: constants, local variables, operations, and the content of the memory cell at an
address. -/
inductive Expr : Type
  | const (n : ℕ)
  | var (x : ℕ)
  | op (o : _root_.Light.Op) (a b : Expr)
  | load (a : Expr)
  deriving Repr

/-- Tests. -/
inductive Cond : Type
  | lt (a b : _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Expr)
  | eq (a b : _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Expr)
  deriving Repr

/-- Statements.  `call p args x` runs procedure number p on the values of args and puts its result
into x. -/
inductive Stmt : Type
  | skip
  | set (x : ℕ) (e : _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Expr)
  | store (a e : _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Expr)
  | seq (s₁ s₂ : Stmt)
  | ite (c : _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Cond) (s₁ s₂ : Stmt)
  | while (c : _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Cond) (s : Stmt)
  | call (p : ℕ) (args : List _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Expr) (x : ℕ)
  deriving Repr

/-- A program: the bodies of its procedures, numbered from 0. -/
abbrev Program : Type := List _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Stmt

/-- What a running procedure sees: its local variables and the memory. -/
structure State : Type where
  loc : ℕ → ℤ
  mem : ℕ → ℤ

/-- The limits on a run: largest absolute value of a word, number of memory cells, nesting depth of
calls. -/
structure Limits : Type where
  word : ℤ
  space : ℕ
  depth : ℕ

/-- The value of an expression. -/
def Expr.val (s : _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.State) : _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Expr → ℤ
  | _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Expr.const n => n
  | _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Expr.var x => s.loc x
  | _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Expr.op o a b => o.eval (a.val s) (b.val s)
  | _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Expr.load a => s.mem (a.val s).toNat

/-- The number of steps that evaluating an expression takes: one for each of its constants,
variables, operations, loads. -/
def Expr.cost : _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Expr → ℕ
  | _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Expr.const _ => 1
  | _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Expr.var _ => 1
  | _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Expr.op _ a b => a.cost + b.cost + 1
  | _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Expr.load a => a.cost + 1

/-- An address within the limits. -/
def Limits.Addr (lim : _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Limits) (a : ℤ) : Prop := 0 ≤ a ∧ a < lim.space

/-- The evaluation of an expression stays within the limits: every value that is formed fits in a
word, and every address that is read is within the memory. -/
def Expr.Safe (lim : _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Limits) (s : _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.State) : _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Expr → Prop
  | _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Expr.const n => (n : ℤ) ≤ lim.word
  | _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Expr.var _ => True
  | _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Expr.op o a b => a.Safe lim s ∧ b.Safe lim s ∧ |o.eval (a.val s) (b.val s)| ≤ lim.word
  | _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Expr.load a => a.Safe lim s ∧ lim.Addr (a.val s)

/-- Whether a test holds. -/
def Cond.Holds (s : _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.State) : _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Cond → Prop
  | _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Cond.lt a b => a.val s < b.val s
  | _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Cond.eq a b => a.val s = b.val s

/-- The number of steps of a test: its two sides and the comparison. -/
def Cond.cost : _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Cond → ℕ
  | _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Cond.lt a b => a.cost + b.cost + 1
  | _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Cond.eq a b => a.cost + b.cost + 1

/-- The evaluation of a test stays within the limits. -/
def Cond.Safe (lim : _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Limits) (s : _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.State) : _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Cond → Prop
  | _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Cond.lt a b => a.Safe lim s ∧ b.Safe lim s
  | _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Cond.eq a b => a.Safe lim s ∧ b.Safe lim s





/-- `Exec lim P d s σ σ' c`: within the limits lim, and at nesting depth d of calls, the statement
s of the program P, started in the state σ, ends in the state σ' after exactly c steps. -/
inductive Exec (lim : _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Limits) (P : _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Program) : ℕ → _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Stmt → _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.State → _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.State → ℕ → Prop
  | skip {d σ} : Exec lim P d _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Stmt.skip σ σ 0
  | set {d σ x e} : e.Safe lim σ →
      Exec lim P d (_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Stmt.set x e) σ { σ with loc := Function.update σ.loc x (e.val σ) } (e.cost + 1)
  | store {d σ a e} : a.Safe lim σ → e.Safe lim σ → lim.Addr (a.val σ) →
      Exec lim P d (_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Stmt.store a e) σ { σ with mem := Function.update σ.mem (a.val σ).toNat (e.val σ) }
        (a.cost + e.cost + 1)
  | seq {d σ σ' σ'' s₁ s₂ c₁ c₂} : Exec lim P d s₁ σ σ' c₁ → Exec lim P d s₂ σ' σ'' c₂ →
      Exec lim P d (_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Stmt.seq s₁ s₂) σ σ'' (c₁ + c₂)
  | iteTrue {d σ σ' c s₁ s₂ k} : c.Safe lim σ → c.Holds σ → Exec lim P d s₁ σ σ' k →
      Exec lim P d (_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Stmt.ite c s₁ s₂) σ σ' (c.cost + 1 + k)
  | iteFalse {d σ σ' c s₁ s₂ k} : c.Safe lim σ → ¬ c.Holds σ → Exec lim P d s₂ σ σ' k →
      Exec lim P d (_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Stmt.ite c s₁ s₂) σ σ' (c.cost + 1 + k)
  | whileFalse {d σ c s} : c.Safe lim σ → ¬ c.Holds σ → Exec lim P d (_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Stmt.while c s) σ σ (c.cost + 1)
  | whileTrue {d σ σ' σ'' c s k₁ k₂} : c.Safe lim σ → c.Holds σ → Exec lim P d s σ σ' k₁ →
      Exec lim P d (_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Stmt.while c s) σ' σ'' k₂ → Exec lim P d (_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Stmt.while c s) σ σ'' (c.cost + 1 + k₁ + k₂)
  | call {d σ σ' p args x body k} : (∀ e ∈ args, e.Safe lim σ) → P[p]? = some body → d < lim.depth →
      Exec lim P (d + 1) body ⟨_root_.Light.frame (args.map (·.val σ)), σ.mem⟩ σ' k →
      Exec lim P d (_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Stmt.call p args x) σ ⟨Function.update σ.loc x (σ'.loc 0), σ'.mem⟩
        ((args.map _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Expr.cost).sum + 2 + k)

/-- Everything held in a variable or in a cell fits in a word. -/
def State.Bounded (lim : _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Limits) (σ : _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.State) : Prop :=
  (∀ x, |σ.loc x| ≤ lim.word) ∧ ∀ a, |σ.mem a| ≤ lim.word

end Light

end

/-!
# Running the word RAM: words, steps, pieces of code, straight-line code, branches

What the proofs about compiled code need to know about the word RAM in which the paper's claims are
stated.

* **Words.**  `wd W v` is the word of the integer v.  If v is in the range of signed words
  (`InRange`), the word gives back v (`toInt_wd`).
* **Steps.**  The end statement defines only whole runs (`exec`).  A configuration (`Cfg`) and a
  single step (`step`) are defined here; `exec_succ_of_step` and `exec_succ_of_verdict` say that
  `exec` takes one step at a time.
* **Runs.**  `Steps P n c c'`: exactly n steps lead from c to c', none of them a verdict.
  Runs are composed by `Steps.trans`; a run that ends before a verdict gives the value of `exec`
  (`exec_of_steps`), and more time does not change that value (`exec_mono`).
* **Code.**  `CodeAt P pos l`: the program P has the instructions of the list l from position pos
  on.
* **Straight-line code.**  Six instructions only change the memory (`Straight`, `effect`); a list
  of them runs through in its length (`steps_straight`).
* **Known numbers.**  On cells that hold the words of known numbers, an instruction writes the word
  of a known number: `effect_add`, …, `effect_store` for the memory; `steps_add`, `steps_sub`,
  `steps_load`, `steps_store` for the step.
* **Branches and verdicts.**  A branch on a cell that holds a known number is `steps_bltz`;
  `Steps.branch` turns its two outcomes into the two outcomes of a test.  The verdicts are
  `step_accept` and `step_reject`.
* **Framing.**  `AgreeOutside s m m'`: the memories m and m' are equal outside the set s of cells.
  For code without stores such a set can be read off the text (`WritesIn`, `agreeOutside_effects`).
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace ThreeSumApsp.WordRam
open _root_.ThreeSumApsp.WordRam

/-!
# Bounds up to a constant factor, in several parameters

The paper writes `f = O(g)` for functions of several parameters that are tied by side conditions,
such as `D ^ 18 ≤ n` for the parameters `n`, `D`, `w`. `Dominated dom f g` says this: there is a
constant `C ≥ 0` with `f x ≤ C * g x` for every tuple `x` of parameters that satisfies `dom x`. If
there is no side condition, `dom` is `fun _ => True`. The type `α` of the parameters is best a
structure with one named field for each of them, so that a bound reads
`Dominated (fun p => p.D ^ 18 ≤ p.n) (fun p => cost p) fun p => p.n ^ 2 / p.D`.

The lemmas of this file are the steps that the paper takes without comment: such bounds can be
chained (`Dominated.trans`), added (`Dominated.add`, `Dominated.add_add`), multiplied and divided
(`Dominated.mul`, `Dominated.mul_left`, `Dominated.const_mul`, `Dominated.pow`,
`Dominated.div_right`), joined by a case distinction (`Dominated.ite`), restricted to a smaller
domain (`Dominated.mono_dom`) and specialized (`Dominated.comp`). With them no proof has to name a
constant. A bound enters the calculus by `Dominated.of_le`, `Dominated.of_le_const_mul` or
`Dominated.of_exists_const`, and leaves it by `obtain ⟨C, hC, hle⟩` or `Dominated.exists_const_and`.
For functions of one natural number, `Dominated.of_eventually` takes a bound for all large `n`,
`Dominated.isBigO` gives Mathlib's `f =O[atTop] g`, and `isBigO_comp_add_one` substitutes a size
that need not tend to infinity.

In every closure lemma the bound comes first and the side conditions follow.

For nonnegative `f` and `g` the notion is Mathlib's `f =O[𝓟 {x | dom x}] g`, big-O along the
principal filter of the domain (`dominated_iff_isBigO_principal`). The one-sided form is taken
because a running time is bounded from above only.

## The notions of "bounded up to a constant" in this library

* `f =O[atTop] g` of Mathlib bounds `|f|` for large `n`. In this sense `IsBigOPow f a` is `O(n^a)`,
  `IsPowPolylog f a` is `O(n^a (log n)^e)` for some `e`, and `IsPowLittleO f a` is `n^{a+o(1)}`.
  The exponents of the theorems are stated with them.
* `UpperBigOPow`, `UpperPowPolylog` and `UpperPowLittleO` are the same three classes as bounds on
  `f` and not on `|f|`, for running times. A two-sided bound gives the one-sided one
  (`IsBigOPow.upperBigOPow`, `IsPowPolylog.upperPowPolylog`, `IsPowLittleO.upperPowLittleO`).
* `Dominated dom f g` bounds `f` on the whole domain, for several parameters. It comes from a bound
  for large `n` by `Dominated.of_eventually` and gives one by `Dominated.isBigO`.
* `Scale.SoftO t e` says that a count `t` with values in `ℕ` is `Dominated` by a monomial with the
  exponents `e`, up to powers of one more quantity; the tactic `growth` reads the exponents off an
  explicit expression. It gives a `Dominated` bound by `Scale.SoftO.dominated`. Its instance
  `SoftOSqrtPow` gives `IsPowPolylog` by `SoftOSqrtPow.isPowPolylog`.
-/

publish_jobs.theorem_title: Tensor recursion, boxes, and word-RAM problem interfaces
publish_jobs.natural_language_statement:
This bundle retains the paper interfaces needed from the formalization of Alman and Vassilevska Williams, *Truly Subquadratic 3SUM and Truly Subcubic APSP via Triangles in Sparse Lopsided Graphs*. The finite alphabets contain seven left variables, seven right variables, ten output variables, and ten terms of Schoenhage's identity. For $i,j\in\{0,1,2\}$, its output forms satisfy $\chi_{P_{ij}}=z_{ij}+z_0$ and $\chi_{P_0}=z_0$. A length-$L$ leaf contributes to an output string exactly when every coordinate contributes.

A cube is a length-$L$ string of terms and stars. If $S(\pi)$ and $Z(\pi)$ are its star and $P_0$ coordinate sets, the box predicate with natural parameters $m,t$ requires

$$|S(\pi)|+|Z(\pi)|\le m-t,\qquad \ell<\ell'\ \text{for every }\ell\in S(\pi),\ \ell'\in Z(\pi).$$

The graph interface has two parts of $n$ vertices, a finite middle part, two adjacency relations, and a finite set of query pairs. The machine interface defines solving a problem on a domain with a real time bound: every permitted input and admissible word size must have a terminating run within that bound, with a correct verdict and output. The derived bound for an integer-magnitude exponent $\kappa\in\mathbb N$, real time exponent $a$, and logarithmic exponent $e\in\mathbb N$ is $C(n^a(\log n)^e+1)$ for some fixed program, word-size slope, and constant $C$; the unrestricted predicate quantifies over every $\kappa$. Thin matrix inputs have dimensions $N\times D$ and $D\times N$, integer entries bounded in absolute value by $U$, and a repetition-free list of requested positions; their encoding stores the dimensions, fixed extra parameters, and row-major matrix entries.

These are specifications and data interfaces, not assertions that the corresponding algorithms already meet their bounds. They connect the combinatorial recursion and its matrix queries to the exact word-RAM semantics used by the complete deterministic integer 3SUM proof.

/-!
# Further statements of the paper

Statements of the paper «Truly Subquadratic 3SUM and Truly Subcubic APSP via Triangles in Sparse
Lopsided Graphs» (Josh Alman, Virginia Vassilevska Williams) beyond the five claims of
`EndStatement.lean`, each as a proposition, with the definitions that they use; and statements that
the notions which this file and `EndStatement.lean` both define agree. The file imports
`EndStatement.lean` and Mathlib. It proves none of the statements: the proofs are in the library,
the folder `ThreeSumApsp/`. The five claims do not depend on this file: it is for a reader who wants
to believe a further lemma, equation, table or theorem of the paper.

`Challenge/PaperStatements.lean` states that the propositions hold: `PaperStatements.lemma_6` says
that `PaperStatements.Lemma_6` holds, and `ThreeSumApsp.wordRam_theorem_5` that the running-time
sentence `ThreeSumApsp.WordRam.Items.Theorem_5` holds.

The parts, in this order:

* Section 2: definitions
* Section 2: statements
* Section 3: definitions
* The reduction of Chan and He: definitions
* Section 3: statements
* Section 4: definitions
* Section 4: statements
* Section 5: definitions
* Section 5: statements
* The word RAM: problems
* Agreement with the definitions of EndStatement.lean
* The word RAM: running times

In a comment, "this part" means the part in which the comment stands.
-/

@[expose] public section

/-!
## Section 2: definitions

Definitions used by the statements of Section 2, "Quickly computing certain entries of a thin matrix
product".  They follow the paper's order and names.  Only what the statements need, directly or
through another definition, is defined here; the other notions of the section, among them the tiling
of Section 2.3.4, are defined with the proofs.

Conventions used throughout.

* The paper numbers indices from 1; Lean's `Fin n` starts at 0.  So the paper's `x₁, x₂, x₃` are
  `LeftVar.x 0, LeftVar.x 1, LeftVar.x 2`, the paper's `p₂₁` is `LeftVar.p 1 0`, and so on.
* A string of length `L` over an alphabet `α` is a function `Fin L → α`.  The paper's level
  `ℓ ∈ {1, …, L}` is the element `ℓ - 1` of `Fin L`; the order of the levels is the order of
  `Fin L`.
* The string `s u'` (the variable `s` followed by the string `u'`) is `Fin.cons s u'`; the first
  variable of `u` is `u 0` and the rest of it is `Fin.tail u`.  The empty string is `Fin.elim0`.
* A linear form is given by the vector of its coefficients: a linear form in the left variables is a
  function `LeftVar → ℤ`.  `Pi.single s 1` is the form consisting of the single variable `s`.
-/

section Sec2Definitions

open _root_.Finset

namespace ThreeSumApsp
open _root_.ThreeSumApsp


/-! ### 2.2 Schönhage's identity for an inner product and an outer product -/

/-- Section 2.2: "We call x₁, x₂, x₃, p₁₁, p₁₂, p₂₁, p₂₂ the seven left variables". -/
inductive LeftVar : Type
  | x (i : Fin 3)
  | p (i j : Fin 2)
  deriving DecidableEq, Fintype

/-- Section 2.2: "and y₁, y₂, y₃, q₁₁, q₁₂, q₂₁, q₂₂ the seven right variables". -/
inductive RightVar : Type
  | y (j : Fin 3)
  | q (i j : Fin 2)
  deriving DecidableEq, Fintype

/-- Section 2.2: "We will also use ten output variables z_ij (for 1 ≤ i, j ≤ 3) and z₀". -/
inductive OutVar : Type
  | z (i j : Fin 3)
  | z0
  deriving DecidableEq, Fintype

/-- Section 2.2: "Schönhage's identity has ten terms, which we name P_ij (for 1 ≤ i, j ≤ 3,
corresponding to the entries of p̂ and q̂) and P₀". -/
inductive Term : Type
  | P (i j : Fin 3)
  | P0
  deriving DecidableEq, Fintype





/-- The linear form consisting of the single output variable `z_ij`. -/
def zForm (i j : Fin 3) : _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSumApsp.OutVar → ℤ := Pi.single (_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSumApsp.OutVar.z i j) 1
/-- The linear form consisting of the single output variable `z₀`. -/

/-- Section 2.2: the linear form `χ_λ` in the output variables,
"χ_{P_ij} = z_ij + z₀" and "χ_{P₀} = z₀". -/
def chi : _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSumApsp.Term → _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSumApsp.OutVar → ℤ
  | _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSumApsp.Term.P i j => _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSumApsp.zForm i j + _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSumApsp.z0Form

## The reduction of Chan and He: definitions

[CH20] is Timothy M. Chan and Qizheng He, *Reducing 3SUM to Convolution-3SUM*, Proc. 3rd SIAM
Symposium on Simplicity in Algorithms (SOSA 2020).  Theorem 21(a) of the paper cites [CH20].  What
is used is the reduction in the proof of its Theorem 5.1, a deterministic reduction from 3SUM to
polylogarithmically many instances of Convolution-3SUM.  The theorem itself is a statement about
running times, for 3SUM on three sets and Convolution-3SUM on three arrays.

This part defines such a reduction, as a function from inputs to lists of instances.  What is proved
about it is stated by `Theorem_21a_threeSum_to_convolution` and `Theorem_21a_threeSum_to_exact`.
The construction follows the proof of Theorem 5.1.  Where it differs from [CH20], and what it adds,
is listed in `docs/REMARKS.md`, "Section 3: cited results".

### Why all these definitions are trusted

The list of instances depends on the input.  A statement of the form "there is a list of instances
such that the input has a solution iff one of them has" would be true for trivial reasons.  So the
statements are about the explicitly defined function `instances`, which is built from `reduction`,
and their worth rests on the definitions of this part.

* `reduction` takes three sets of at most n integers.  It returns the nodes of a recursion tree, and
  each node stands for one instance of Convolution-3SUM on three arrays.  3SUM on three sets (are
  there a, b, c, one from each set, with a + b + c = 0?) and Convolution-3SUM on three arrays (are
  there i, j with X i + Y j = Z (i + j)?) are the problems of Definitions 2.1 and 2.2 of [CH20], for
  which Theorem 5.1 is stated.
* `instances` takes n numbers, for the problem whether three of them, at three different positions,
  sum to 0.  It returns instances of Convolution-3SUM on one array.  These are the problems of the
  paper, 3SUM in the reading fixed at `ThreeSum`.

Evaluated literally, `coll` and `heavy` compare all pairs of elements, and each search tests all its
candidates, so the definitions are a specification and not the algorithm.  Nothing in this part is
about a machine.

Every choice that the two functions make depends only on which elements collide and how many pairs
do, on which sets are empty, on binary digits of the numbers and on how often a number occurs.  None
depends on whether a solution exists, with one exception: the solution 0, 0, 0 exists exactly when 0
occurs at three positions.  So it is detected by counting, and it is reported through the three-set
input (`zeroSet x`, {0}, {0}), which has a solution exactly in that case.

In this part `ν` is a node of the recursion tree.  It is not the exponent ν of Theorem 21, which
the statements call `κ`.

/-! ### What it means to solve a problem

**The order of the choices.**  In every statement the order is: the constants of the problem (the
exponent `κ` of the magnitude of the numbers, the `k` of `k`-Clique); then the program, the slope
`b` of the word size and the constant `C` of the time bound; then the instance; then the word size,
any number of bits that is admissible for the slope.  So the program cannot depend on the instance
or on its size, and it cannot rely on long words. -/

/-! #### The word size and the output cells -/





/-! #### Problems, and solving a problem within a time bound -/



/-- **Solving a problem within a time bound.**  The program `P` with slope `b` solves the problem on
the instances in `dom` within time `T`: on every such instance `x` and at every admissible word size
`bits`, the run from the first instruction on the starting memory (input in the cells 0, 1, 2, …,
zeros elsewhere) gives a verdict after at most `T x` steps, and the verdict and the output are a
correct answer. -/
def Solves (prob : _root_.ThreeSumApsp.WordRam.Problem) (P : List _root_.EndStatement.Instr) (b : ℕ) (dom : prob.Inst → Prop) (T : prob.Inst → ℝ) :
    Prop :=
  ∀ x : prob.Inst, dom x → ∀ bits : ℕ, _root_.ThreeSumApsp.WordRam.Admissible b (prob.params x) bits →
    ∃ (t : ℕ) (verdict : Bool) (c : ℤ → BitVec bits), (t : ℝ) ≤ T x ∧
      _root_.EndStatement.exec P t 0 (_root_.EndStatement.loadWords bits (prob.input x)) = some (verdict, c) ∧
      prob.IsAnswer x verdict (_root_.ThreeSumApsp.WordRam.output c (prob.input x).length)

/-! #### Time bounds in one size `n`, for the problems of `EndStatement.lean` -/



/-- The problem `Q`, a value of `EndStatement.Problem`, is solved by a deterministic algorithm in
`O(n^a (log n)^e)` time when all numbers are integers of absolute value at most `n^κ`: there are a
program, a slope and a constant `C` such that the program solves `Q` within `C (n^a (log n)^e + 1)`
steps.  (For `a ≥ 0` the `+ 1` matters only at `n ≤ 1`, where `n^a (log n)^e` may be 0.) -/
def SolvedInTimeAt (Q : _root_.EndStatement.Problem) (κ : ℕ) (a : ℝ) (e : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (P : List _root_.EndStatement.Instr) (b : ℕ) (C : ℝ),
    _root_.ThreeSumApsp.WordRam.SolvesWithin Q κ P b fun n => C * ((n : ℝ) ^ a * Real.log n ^ e + 1)

/-- The same for every constant `κ`: "all numbers in the input are integers of absolute value
n^{O(1)}" (Theorem 2).  The program, the slope and the constant may depend on `κ`.

NOTE.  `κ` is the paper's ν.  Where the paper has ν ≥ 1 (Theorem 19, Corollary 39), `κ = 0` is
included here. -/
def SolvedInTime (Q : _root_.EndStatement.Problem) (a : ℝ) (e : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ κ : ℕ, _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSumApsp.WordRam.SolvedInTimeAt Q κ a e





/-! #### A query program that serves one query after the other -/





/-! #### Programs that receive their input in phases

A problem in phases has one program for each phase.  The inputs of the phases are laid
out one after the other in the cells 0, 1, 2, …, but the input of a phase is written into its cells
only when the phase starts.  Each program starts at its first instruction on the memory that the
previous phase has left; the first one starts on a memory of zeros.  So a phase cannot see the input
of a later phase, and nothing is reset between phases.  The output is read from the cells after the
last input.  Receiving an input takes no steps, and the inputs of earlier phases stay in memory
unless a program overwrites them.  What an earlier phase has left in the cells of a later input is
lost; the earlier phase knows which cells these are, since all sizes are given in Phase 1.  (In the
running times of Corollary 40 the bound of a phase is at least the length of its input, if the
exponent `γ` of `Items.Corollary_40_general_times` is at most 1; so they do not depend on inputs
being free.) -/







/-! ### The problems of the paper, their inputs and their answers

**Layout.**  Matrices are written row by row, one number per cell, as signed words.  Booleans are
written as 0 and 1, and indices and vertices count from 0.  The first cells hold the sizes.  The
bound on the absolute values of the numbers is not written into memory.  For the matrix problems it
is a number `U` that is part of the instance as a mathematical object (`ThinPair`); for the problems
in the form of `EndStatement.Problem` it is a hypothesis of `SolvesWithin`.  In the statements it is
a fixed power of the size, with an exponent that is fixed before the program (and 1 for the 0/1
matrices of the lopsided triangle problems).  A program for a problem with an output has to accept,
and to leave the output in the cells right after the input. -/

/-! #### How matrices and Booleans are written -/





/-! #### The wanted entries of a thin matrix product (Theorems 1, 5, 25 and 30, Corollaries 26 and
32) -/

/-- Two matrices `X ∈ ℤ^{N×D}` and `Y ∈ ℤ^{D×N}` with entries of absolute value at most `U`. -/
structure ThinPair where
  /-- The long side. -/
  N : ℕ
  /-- The short side. -/
  D : ℕ
  /-- The bound on the absolute values of the entries. -/
  U : ℕ
  /-- The first matrix. -/
  X : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin D) ℤ
  /-- The second matrix. -/
  Y : Matrix (Fin D) (Fin N) ℤ
  /-- The entries of `X` are bounded. -/
  boundX : ∀ i j, |X i j| ≤ (U : ℤ)
  /-- The entries of `Y` are bounded. -/
  boundY : ∀ i j, |Y i j| ≤ (U : ℤ)

/-- Theorem 5: two such matrices and "a set W of [...] positions of an N × N matrix".

NOTE.  The paper does not say how a set is given.  Here it is a list without repetitions, in any
order. -/
structure ThinInstance extends _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSumApsp.WordRam.ThinPair where

publish_jobs.theorem_title: Certified logarithm intervals for the integer schedule
publish_jobs.natural_language_statement:
For a natural truncation index $n$ and a real number $z$, define the finite odd-power sum

$$S_n(z)=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}\frac{z^{2i+1}}{2i+1}.$$

The supporting interval certificate applies when $0\le z<1$ and $y=(1+z)/(1-z)$. If real endpoints $L,U$ satisfy $L\le2S_n(z)$ and $2(S_n(z)+z^{2n+1}/(1-z^2))\le U$, it yields $L\le\log y\le U$. The bundle instantiates this certificate with explicit rational endpoints of denominator $10^{22}$ for $\log2$, $\log(29/16)$, $\log(232/231)$, $\log(464/463)$, $\log(32\theta)$, and $\log(2(1-\theta))$, where $\theta$ is the fixed rational analysis parameter. It also supplies decidability of the cleared integer switching predicate for natural parameters $J,s,j,q$.

These finite certificates make the numerical exponent and switching estimates available without floating-point assumptions in the deterministic integer 3SUM runtime proof. The finite-minimum and rounding machinery adapts the pinned upstream Switch formalization.

publish_jobs.theorem_title: Certified logarithm intervals for the integer schedule
publish_jobs.natural_language_statement:
For a natural truncation index $n$ and a real number $z$, define the finite odd-power sum

$$S_n(z)=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}\frac{z^{2i+1}}{2i+1}.$$

The supporting interval certificate applies when $0\le z<1$ and $y=(1+z)/(1-z)$. If real endpoints $L,U$ satisfy $L\le2S_n(z)$ and $2(S_n(z)+z^{2n+1}/(1-z^2))\le U$, it yields $L\le\log y\le U$. The bundle instantiates this certificate with explicit rational endpoints of denominator $10^{22}$ for $\log2$, $\log(29/16)$, $\log(232/231)$, $\log(464/463)$, $\log(32\theta)$, and $\log(2(1-\theta))$, where $\theta$ is the fixed rational analysis parameter. It also supplies decidability of the cleared integer switching predicate for natural parameters $J,s,j,q$.

These finite certificates make the numerical exponent and switching estimates available without floating-point assumptions in the deterministic integer 3SUM runtime proof. The finite-minimum and rounding machinery adapts the pinned upstream Switch formalization.

publish_jobs.theorem_title: Entropy, quartic integer switch, twelve costs and fixed-expansion model
publish_jobs.natural_language_statement:
Defines binary entropy in bits $H(t)$, $E_c=(c/2)H(1/c)$, $\kappa_c=2cH(1/(2c))-cH(1/c)-1$, and $\gamma_c(t)=cH(1/c)-cH((1-t)/c)$ for natural expansion $c$. The quartic is $P(t)=7.85174904t+0.72447023t^2+0.24044466t^3+0.12022459t^4$, with its polynomial derivative. The fixed rational parameters are $e=0.203889696$, $b=-0.062656016$, $S=0.193175570$, $\theta=0.040409899$, $\tau=13/20$, $\rho=0.27905030$, and $u=0.17200068185091493$. The principal cost cap is $1.96061388$ and the campaign target is the rational $1.960614$.

The ledger lists all twelve source costs in their source order. `costs` instantiates them at the fixed parameters and $c=232$. The natural-number predicate `clearedSwitch` is the degree-four integer comparison of Section 4.2, with $v=S-2b=159243801/500000000$. `ModelFeasible` describes the relaxed fixed-expansion real cost model, including its whole-interval entropy inequality and all twelve charges. It is not a model of arbitrary 3SUM algorithms. Total logarithms, division and natural subtraction are unrestricted in these definitions; theorem hypotheses delimit the intended domains. The shared machine and decision-problem definitions are imported unchanged.

import Mathlib

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false

noncomputable section

namespace ThreeSum1960614

noncomputable def entropy (t : ℝ) : ℝ := Real.binEntropy t / Real.log 2
noncomputable def E (c : ℕ) : ℝ := (c : ℝ) / 2 * entropy (1 / c)
noncomputable def kappa (c : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  2 * c * entropy (1 / (2 * c)) - c * entropy (1 / c) - 1
noncomputable def gamma (c : ℕ) (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  c * entropy (1 / c) - c * entropy ((1 - t) / c)
def phi (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (785174904 * t + 72447023 * t ^ 2 + 24044466 * t ^ 3 + 12022459 * t ^ 4) / 100000000
def phiDeriv (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (785174904 + 2 * 72447023 * t + 3 * 24044466 * t ^ 2 + 4 * 12022459 * t ^ 3) / 100000000
def epsilon : ℝ := 203889696 / 1000000000
def beta : ℝ := -(62656016 / 1000000000)
def saving : ℝ := 193175570 / 1000000000
def theta : ℝ := 40409899 / 1000000000
def tau : ℝ := 13 / 20
def rho : ℝ := 2790503 / 10000000
def tangentPoint : ℝ := 17200068185091493 / 100000000000000000
def principal : ℝ := 196061388 / 100000000
def target : ℚ := 1960614 / 1000000
def v : ℝ := saving - 2 * beta
def threshold (a : ℝ) : ℝ := (v + a) / (1 - a)
def ledger (e b S terminal ratio EE kk hh : ℝ) : List ℝ :=
  [2 * e * EE,
   1 + e * (EE - b),
   2 - e * S,
   2 - e * (1 / 2 + b - hh),
   2 - e * (1 / 2 - b - kk - ratio * (1 + S - 2 * b)),
   2 - e * (terminal - 1 / 2 - b - kk),
   e * (8 / 5) * (EE + 1 / 2),
   2 + e * (4 / 5 - (2 / 5) * EE - 2 * b),
   1 + e * (1 / 2 - b),
   2 - e * (EE + b),
   2 - 2 * e * (EE + b), 1]
noncomputable def costs : List ℝ :=
  ledger epsilon beta saving tau rho (E 232) (kappa 232) (entropy theta)
def clearedSwitch (J s j q : ℕ) : Prop :=
  let r := (J - j) * s
  500000000 * (J - j) *
    (785174904 * q * r ^ 3 + 72447023 * q ^ 2 * r ^ 2 +
     24044466 * q ^ 3 * r + 12022459 * q ^ 4) ≥
    100000000 * (159243801 * J + 500000000 * j) * r ^ 4
noncomputable def ModelFeasible (c : ℕ) (e b S th terminal ratio R : ℝ) : Prop :=
  0 < e ∧ e < 1 ∧ b < 0 ∧ 0 < S ∧
  0 ≤ th ∧ th ≤ 1 / 2 ∧ 0 ≤ terminal ∧ terminal < 1 ∧
  0 < ratio ∧ S - 2 * b ≤ gamma c th ∧
  (∀ t ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) (1 / 2), entropy t ≤ ratio * (1 + gamma c t)) ∧
  ∀ z ∈ ledger e b S terminal ratio (E c) (kappa c) (entropy th), z ≤ R

end ThreeSum1960614

publish_jobs.theorem_title: Deterministic integer 3SUM in O(n^1.999017) word-RAM steps
publish_jobs.formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSumSharpTail.threeSum_1999017 :
    EndStatement.ThreeSum.SolvedInTime 1.999017 := by sorry
publish_jobs.natural_language_statement:
For each fixed $\kappa\in\mathbb N$, there exist a finite deterministic word-RAM program $P$, a natural number $b$, and a step bound $T:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$. For every $n$, input $x:\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\to\mathbb Z$ with $|x_i|\le n^\kappa$, and every $W\ge b(\operatorname{Nat.log2}(n)+1)$, the program halts within $T(n)$ steps and accepts exactly when three pairwise distinct indices have sum zero. Equal values at distinct indices are allowed; no witness is required; inputs of size less than three are rejected.

The exact time requirement is $\exists K\in\mathbb N\;\forall n\ge2,\ T(n)^{1000000}\le K n^{1999017}$, equivalent to $T(n)=O(n^{1.999017})$. The target instantiates the campaign template without changing its definitions.

Source: Theorem 1.1 of Xu's sharp-tail manuscript. The manuscript states $\kappa\ge1$ and a sufficiently large logarithmic word width; the campaign additionally makes uniformity over all larger widths explicit. The case $\kappa=0$ follows from the $\kappa=1$ bound for $n\ge1$, with $n=0$ handled separately. The formal development must justify this interface adaptation. The improved bound is a proposed formalization target, not an already Lean-certified result.

publish_jobs.formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSumSharpTail.admissible_parameters_solve_3sum
    (c : ℕ) (θ : ℝ) (a s r : ℚ) (hc : 10 < c)
    (hθ0 : 0 < θ) (hθ9 : θ < 9 / 10)
    (ha0 : 0 < a) (ha1 : a < 1) (hs0 : 0 < s) (hs1 : s < 1)
    (henc : (a : ℝ) * (ThreeSumSharpTail.encodingExponent c + ThreeSumSharpTail.sharpSaving c θ) < 1)
    (hprep : (s : ℝ) < ThreeSumSharpTail.sharpSaving c θ)
    (hquery : (s : ℝ) < 1 / 2 - ThreeSumSharpTail.queryExponent θ)
    (hprime : Real.log 7 / Real.log 2 + 3 * (a : ℝ) / 2 < 3 - (a : ℝ) * s / 2)
    (hbuild : 2 + (a : ℝ) * (1 + (s : ℝ) / 2) < 3 - (a : ℝ) * s / 2)
    (hr : 2 - a * s / 4 < r) :
    EndStatement.ThreeSum.SolvedInTime r := by sorry
publish_jobs.natural_language_statement:
Let $c>10$ be an integer, $0<\theta<0.9$, and let $a,s,r$ be rational with $0<a<1$ and $0<s<1$. Suppose
$$a(A(c)+\gamma_*(c,\theta))<1,\qquad s<\gamma_*(c,\theta),\qquad s<\tfrac12-q(\theta),$$
$$\log_2 7+\tfrac32a<3-as/2,\qquad 2+a(1+s/2)<3-as/2,\qquad r>2-as/4.$$
Then deterministic integer 3SUM satisfies the campaign's exact shared predicate `EndStatement.ThreeSum.SolvedInTime r`. This is the combined consequence of Propositions 4.1 and 5.1, not a verbatim separate proposition in the manuscript. Its proof must construct the word-RAM program and establish correctness and all costs using the inherited algorithms and reductions. No inner-algorithm oracle or correctness assumption is supplied as a hypothesis. The uniform word-width requirement in the shared specification is part of the formalization obligation.

publish_jobs.theorem_title: Entropy, box counts, and cost exponents for the sharp-tail analysis
publish_jobs.natural_language_statement: Defines $H(x)=-x\log x-(1-x)\log(1-x)$ (so $H(0)=H(1)=0$), the old preprocessing saving $\gamma(c,\theta)=\theta\log((c-1)/9)/\log4$, the sharp saving $\gamma_*(c,\theta)=[cH(1/c)-cH((1-\theta)/c)-\theta\log9]/\log4$, the query exponent $q(\theta)=[H(\theta)+\theta\log9]/\log4$, and the encoding exponent $A(c)=[c\log10-cH(1/c)/2-(c-1)\log3]/\log4$. For natural numbers $c,m,d$, defines $\beta_d=\binom{cm}{m-d}9^{cm-m+d}$; later lemmas restrict to $c>10$, $m\ge1$ and $d\le m$. These are auxiliary analytic quantities, not a replacement for the campaign's shared word-RAM or 3SUM definitions. Real logarithms and division are total in Lean; intended domains are supplied by theorem hypotheses.
publish_jobs.definitions:
import Mathlib

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false

namespace ThreeSumSharpTail

noncomputable def entropy (x : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  -x * Real.log x - (1 - x) * Real.log (1 - x)

noncomputable def oldSaving (c θ : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  θ * Real.log ((c - 1) / 9) / Real.log 4

noncomputable def sharpSaving (c θ : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (c * entropy (1 / c) - c * entropy ((1 - θ) / c) - θ * Real.log 9) / Real.log 4

noncomputable def queryExponent (θ : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (entropy θ + θ * Real.log 9) / Real.log 4

noncomputable def encodingExponent (c : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (c * Real.log 10 - c * entropy (1 / c) / 2 - (c - 1) * Real.log 3) / Real.log 4

def boxCount (c m d : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  Nat.choose (c * m) (m - d) * 9 ^ (c * m - m + d)

end ThreeSumSharpTail

noncomputable def periodCoordinate (j : ℕ) (ω : ℂ) : PowerSeries ℂ :=

namespace OAI.PiExponent.MatrixTranslation

open scoped BigOperators
open MvPolynomial
open RowTranslation

noncomputable def transverseIndices {m : ℕ} (w : Fin m → ℝ) (H : ℝ) :

namespace OAI.PiExponent.RowTranslation

open scoped BigOperators
open MvPolynomial
variable {σ : Type*} [Fintype σ] [DecidableEq σ]

abbrev RowChoices (S : Finset (σ →₀ ℕ)) (β : σ →₀ ℕ) (s : ℕ) :=
  Σ a : S, (∀ i, Fin (a.1 i - β i + 1)) × Fin (s + 1)

end OAI.PiExponent.RowTranslation

namespace OAI.PiExponent.RowTranslation

open scoped BigOperators
open MvPolynomial
variable {σ R : Type*} [Fintype σ] [DecidableEq σ] [CommRing R]

noncomputable def rowScalar (ε : σ → R) (τ : σ → PowerSeries R)
    (β a : σ →₀ ℕ) (d : ∀ i, Fin (a i - β i + 1)) (k : ℕ) : R :=
  ((∏ i, (a i).choose (β i) * (a i - β i).choose (d i) : ℕ) : R) *
    (∏ i, ε i ^ (a i - β i - d i)) *
      PowerSeries.coeff k (∏ i, τ i ^ (d i : ℕ))

end OAI.PiExponent.RowTranslation

namespace OAI.PiExponent.RowTranslation

open scoped BigOperators
open MvPolynomial
variable {R : Type*} [CommRing R]

noncomputable def tail (T : ℕ) (f : PowerSeries R) : PowerSeries R :=
  (PowerSeries.trunc T f : PowerSeries R) - f

end OAI.PiExponent.RowTranslation

namespace OAI.PiExponent



noncomputable def logarithmicPeriod : ℂ := 2 * (Real.pi : ℂ) * Complex.I

end OAI.PiExponent

namespace OAI.PiExponent.LiteralAnalytic

open scoped BigOperators
open DeterminantContradiction

abbrev RowChoice {nu : ℝ} (d : FixedData nu) (H : ℝ) (r : Row d H) :=
  RowTranslation.RowChoices (MatrixTranslation.transverseIndices (fixedWeights d) H)
    (beta d r) (r.2.1 0)

end OAI.PiExponent.LiteralAnalytic

namespace OAI.PiExponent.LiteralAnalytic

open scoped BigOperators
open DeterminantContradiction

abbrev Transverse {nu : ℝ} (d : FixedData nu) (H : ℝ) :=

end OAI.PiExponent.LiteralAnalytic

namespace OAI.PiExponent.LiteralAnalytic

open scoped BigOperators
open DeterminantContradiction

noncomputable def rowWeight {nu : ℝ} (d : FixedData nu) {H : ℝ} (r : Row d H) : ℝ :=
  MatrixTranslationBounds.weight (fixedWeights d) (fun i => beta d r i)

end OAI.PiExponent.LiteralAnalytic

namespace OAI.PiExponent.MatrixTranslation

open scoped BigOperators
open MvPolynomial
open RowTranslation

noncomputable def periodMonomial {m : ℕ} (j : ℕ) (ω : ℂ) (h : ℕ)
    (a : Fin m → ℕ) : MvPolynomial (Fin m) (PowerSeries ℂ) :=
  C ((1 + PowerSeries.X) ^ h) *
    ∏ i, (C (periodCoordinate j ω) + X i) ^ a i

end OAI.PiExponent.MatrixTranslation

namespace OAI.PiExponent.LiteralAnalytic

open scoped BigOperators
open DeterminantContradiction

abbrev ChoiceFamily {nu : ℝ} (d : FixedData nu) (H : ℝ) :=
  ∀ r : Row d H, RowChoice d H r

end OAI.PiExponent.LiteralAnalytic

namespace OAI.PiExponent.LiteralAnalytic

open scoped BigOperators
open DeterminantContradiction

noncomputable def choiceScalar {nu : ℝ} (d : FixedData nu) {H : ℝ}
    (r : Row d H) (t : RowChoice d H r) : ℂ :=
  RowTranslation.rowScalar
    (fun i => (r.1.val : ℂ) *
      (MatrixArithmetic.rationalCenters (finiteNumerators d) (finiteDenominators d) i - logarithmicPeriod))
    (fun i => RowTranslation.tail
      (MatrixArithmetic.truncationOrders (finiteDenominators d) d.F0 d.v0 i) (PowerSeries.log ℂ))
    (beta d r) t.1.1 t.2.1 t.2.2

end OAI.PiExponent.LiteralAnalytic

namespace OAI.PiExponent.LiteralAnalytic

open scoped BigOperators
open DeterminantContradiction

noncomputable def indexWeight {nu : ℝ} (d : FixedData nu) {H : ℝ} (a : Transverse d H) : ℝ :=
  MatrixTranslationBounds.weight (fixedWeights d) (fun i => a.1 i)

end OAI.PiExponent.LiteralAnalytic

namespace OAI.PiExponent.LiteralAnalytic

open scoped BigOperators
open DeterminantContradiction

noncomputable def choiceMatrix {nu : ℝ} (d : FixedData nu) {H : ℝ}
    (selection : Row d H → Column d H) (f : ChoiceFamily d H) : Matrix (Row d H) (Row d H) ℂ :=
  fun r c => PowerSeries.coeff (r.2.1 0 - (f r).2.2)
    ((MatrixTranslation.periodMonomial r.1.val logarithmicPeriod
      ((selection c).1 0) (fun i => (selection c).1 i.succ)).coeff (f r).1.1)

end OAI.PiExponent.LiteralAnalytic

publish_jobs.natural_language_statement:
Define $r=\exp(-\log 2/2)$, the collision remainder $C(M,H)=(\log M+\log 2/4-\log(1-r))/H$, and the translation term count $T(m,v,H)=(\lfloor H\rfloor_{\mathbb N}+1)^{2m}(\lfloor H/v\rfloor_{\mathbb N}+1)$. For the original fixed admissible data $d$ with row count $M_d(H)$, define

$$R_d(H)=C(M_d(H),H)+\frac{\log T(d.m,d.v_0,H)}{H}.$$

Here $M,m$ are natural numbers and $v,H$ are real. The natural floor is the original source operation; the definitions impose no positivity hypotheses and assert no convergence or determinant estimate. These exact quantities state the two immediate original children of the analytic aggregate theorem.

  (Real.log M + Real.log 2 / 4 - Real.log (1 - collisionRatio)) / H

namespace OAI.PiExponent

noncomputable def translationTermCount (m : ℕ) (v H : ℝ) : ℕ :=
  (⌊H⌋₊ + 1) ^ (2 * m) * (⌊H / v⌋₊ + 1)

    Real.log (translationTermCount d.m d.v0 H : ℝ) / H

theorem OAI.PiExponent.DeterminantAnalyticBound.translated_summand_bound
    {ι κ : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ]
    (group : ι → κ) (weight : κ → ℝ) (scalar determinant : ℂ)
    {H A eta nu c N bbar Etr Ehol rho : ℝ}
    (hH : 0 < H) (hA : 0 ≤ A) (heta : 0 ≤ eta) (hnu : 0 ≤ nu)
    (hc : 0 ≤ c) (hN : 0 < N) (hw : ∀ a, 0 ≤ weight a)
    (hbeta : (Fintype.card ι : ℝ) * H * bbar ≤ ∑ i, weight (group i))
    (hcap : (((Finset.univ : Finset κ).filter (fun a => weight a ≤ A * H)).card : ℝ) ≤ N)
    (hscalar : ‖scalar‖ ≤ Real.exp
      (-nu * ((∑ i, weight (group i)) - (Fintype.card ι : ℝ) * H * bbar) +
        (Fintype.card ι : ℝ) * H * Etr))
    (hdet : ‖determinant‖ ≤ Real.exp
      (-c * (∑ a, (Collision.multiplicity Finset.univ group a : ℝ) ^ 2) +
        (Fintype.card ι : ℝ) * H * (Ehol + rho))) :
    ‖scalar * determinant‖ ≤ Real.exp ((Fintype.card ι : ℝ) * H *
      (Etr + Ehol + rho + max (-c * eta ^ 2 * (Fintype.card ι : ℝ) / (H * N))
        (-nu * (A * (1 - eta) - bbar)))) := by
  sorry
publish_jobs.natural_language_statement:
Let finite index types $\iota,\kappa$, a grouping $g:\iota\to\kappa$, nonnegative group weights $w$, and complex numbers $s,d$ satisfy the original scalar and determinant exponential bounds. Assume $H,N>0$, $A,\eta,\nu,c\ge0$, total weight at least $|\iota|H\bar b$, and at most $N$ groups of weight at most $AH$. Then

$$\|sd\|\le \exp\!\left(|\iota|H\left[E_{\mathrm{tr}}+E_{\mathrm{hol}}+\rho+\max\!\left\{-\frac{c\eta^2|\iota|}{HN},-\nu(A(1-\eta)-\bar b)\right\}\right]\right).$$

The determinant hypothesis contains the collision occupancy sum $\sum_{a\in\kappa}m(g,a)^2$, where $m(g,a)=\#\{i:g(i)=a\}$. The scalar hypothesis contains $-\nu(\sum_i w(g(i))-|\iota|H\bar b)+|\iota|HE_{\mathrm{tr}}$, and the determinant hypothesis contains $-c\sum_a m(g,a)^2+|\iota|H(E_{\mathrm{hol}}+\rho)$. No sign assumption on $E_{\mathrm{tr}},E_{\mathrm{hol}},\rho,\bar b$ is added.

publish_jobs.theorem_title: Column and row scales, clearing denominator and logarithmic costs
publish_jobs.natural_language_statement:
Let $q_i$ be natural denominators and let $a,b$ be natural exponent vectors on $m$ coordinates. Put $w_i=\lceil\log q_i\rceil_+$, where the ceiling is natural. Define the column scale, inverse row scale, and common denominator at real height $H$ and natural truncation orders $T_i$ by

$$C_q(a)=\prod_i q_i^{a_i},\qquad R_q(b)=C_q(b)^{-1},\qquad D(q,T,H)=\prod_i\operatorname{lcm}(1,\ldots,T_i)^{\lfloor H/w_i\rfloor_+}.$$

For the original finite row domain $\mathcal R=\mathrm{Row}(K,v_0,\theta,w,H)$ and a column selection $\kappa:\mathcal R\to\mathrm{Column}(w_0,w,H)$, define the logarithmic costs

$$B=\sum_{\rho\in\mathcal R}\sum_i b_{\rho,i}\log q_i,\qquad A_\kappa=\sum_{\rho\in\mathcal R}\sum_i a_{\kappa(\rho),i}\log q_i.$$

Here $K$ is natural and $w_0,v_0,\theta,H$ are real domain parameters; $b_{\rho,i}$ and $a_{\kappa(\rho),i}$ are the nonconstant coordinates of the row and selected column exponent vectors. All five quantities are real and are defined without positivity assumptions, using the original finite domains. They provide the scaling and cost data for determinant denominator clearing.
publish_jobs.definitions:
import Definitions.Def_OAI_NumberTheory_PiExponent_Approximation_MatrixArithmetic_CoreData

namespace OAI.PiExponent.MatrixArithmetic

open scoped BigOperators

noncomputable def columnScale {m : ℕ} (q : Fin m → ℕ) (a : Fin m → ℕ) : ℝ :=
  ∏ i, (q i : ℝ) ^ a i

noncomputable def rowScale {m : ℕ} (q : Fin m → ℕ) (b : Fin m → ℕ) : ℝ :=
  (columnScale q b)⁻¹

noncomputable def denominator {m : ℕ} (q : Fin m → ℕ) (T : Fin m → ℕ) (H : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∏ i, (Nat.lcmUpto (T i) : ℝ) ^ ⌊H / logWeights q i⌋₊

noncomputable def rowCost {m : ℕ} (K : ℕ) (v0 θ : ℝ)
    (q : Fin m → ℕ) (H : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ ρ : InterpolationMatrix.Row K v0 θ (logWeights q) H,
    ∑ i, (ρ.2.1 i.succ : ℝ) * Real.log (q i)

noncomputable def columnCost {m : ℕ} {K : ℕ} {w0 v0 θ : ℝ}
    (q : Fin m → ℕ) {H : ℝ}
    (selection : InterpolationMatrix.Row K v0 θ (logWeights q) H →
      InterpolationMatrix.Column w0 (logWeights q) H) : ℝ :=
  ∑ ρ : InterpolationMatrix.Row K v0 θ (logWeights q) H,
    ∑ i, ((selection ρ).1 i.succ : ℝ) * Real.log (q i)

end OAI.PiExponent.MatrixArithmetic

publish_jobs.natural_language_statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative semiring and $\sigma$ an index type. For $c:\sigma\to R$, define the polynomial translation homomorphism and its monomial coefficient by

$$\tau_c(X_i)=X_i+c_i,\qquad S_c(\beta,a)=[X^\beta]\tau_c(X^a).$$

Here $a,\beta:\sigma\to_0\mathbb N$ are finitely supported exponent vectors. When $\sigma$ is finite, the finite multi-index map converts $a:\sigma\to\mathbb N$ to the same vector viewed as a finitely supported function. These are the original data used to expand shifted interpolation polynomials.

publish_jobs.theorem_title: Fixed-data interfaces for the determinant contradiction
publish_jobs.natural_language_statement:
For a real approximation exponent $\nu$, let fixed data be admissible parameters with the source arithmetic constant and collision constant $c=\log(2)/4$. Write $M(H)$ for the row count, $N(H)$ for the low-index count, and $b(H)$ for the normalized weighted row mean. Define the associated matrix, selected minor, and

$$\gamma(H)=\frac{c\eta^2M(H)}{H N(H)},\qquad \gamma_\infty=\frac{c\eta^2K\theta^m}{(m+1)v_0A^m}.$$

The global interpolation hypothesis asserts that, for every $\nu>2$, every fixed datum and every real lower height, some larger height has a surjective matrix linear map. The analytic aggregate hypothesis asserts that every such datum admits an error tending to zero whose eventual determinant bound is the exact source analytic-and-collision estimate. These are the original quantified interfaces for the conditional determinant contradiction.

namespace OAI.PiExponent.DeterminantContradiction

open Filter
open scoped Topology

abbrev FixedData (nu : ℝ) := AdmissibleParameters nu Arithmetic.lcmConstant collisionConstant

noncomputable def finiteNumerators {nu : ℝ} (d : FixedData nu) : Fin d.m → ℤ :=
  fun i => d.p i.val

noncomputable def finiteDenominators {nu : ℝ} (d : FixedData nu) : Fin d.m → ℕ :=
  fun i => d.q i.val

abbrev Row {nu : ℝ} (d : FixedData nu) (H : ℝ) :=
  InterpolationMatrix.Row d.K d.v0 d.base.theta
    (MatrixArithmetic.logWeights (finiteDenominators d)) H

abbrev Column {nu : ℝ} (d : FixedData nu) (H : ℝ) :=
  InterpolationMatrix.Column d.w0 (MatrixArithmetic.logWeights (finiteDenominators d)) H

noncomputable def actualMatrix {nu : ℝ} (d : FixedData nu) (H : ℝ) :
    Matrix (Row d H) (Column d H) ℂ :=
  InterpolationMatrix.truncatedLogMatrix d.K d.w0 d.v0 d.base.theta
    (MatrixArithmetic.logWeights (finiteDenominators d)) H
    (MatrixArithmetic.rationalCenters (finiteNumerators d) (finiteDenominators d))
    (MatrixArithmetic.truncationOrders (finiteDenominators d) d.F0 d.v0)

noncomputable def actualMinor {nu : ℝ} (d : FixedData nu) (H : ℝ)
    (selection : Row d H → Column d H) : Matrix (Row d H) (Row d H) ℂ :=
  MatrixArithmetic.selectedMinor d.K d.w0 d.v0 d.base.theta d.F0 H
    (finiteNumerators d) (finiteDenominators d) selection

noncomputable def actualMean {nu : ℝ} (d : FixedData nu) (H : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  MatrixArithmetic.meanRowWeight d.K d.v0 d.base.theta (finiteDenominators d) H

noncomputable def actualRowCount {nu : ℝ} (d : FixedData nu) (H : ℝ) : ℕ :=
  Fintype.card (Row d H)

noncomputable def lowIndexCount {nu : ℝ} (d : FixedData nu) (H : ℝ) : ℕ :=
  (realWeightedSimplex (MatrixArithmetic.logWeights (finiteDenominators d))
    ((d.base.A : ℝ) * H)).card

noncomputable def collisionRate {nu : ℝ} (d : FixedData nu) (H : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  collisionConstant * d.base.eta ^ 2 * (actualRowCount d H : ℝ) /
    (H * (lowIndexCount d H : ℝ))

noncomputable def collisionLimit {nu : ℝ} (d : FixedData nu) : ℝ :=
  collisionConstant *
    (d.base.eta ^ 2 * (d.K : ℝ) * (d.base.theta : ℝ) ^ d.m /
      (((d.m : ℝ) + 1) * (d.v0 : ℝ) * (d.base.A : ℝ) ^ d.m))

def GlobalInterpolationStatement : Prop :=
  ∀ nu : ℝ, 2 < nu → ∀ d : FixedData nu,
    ∀ L : ℝ, ∃ H : ℝ, L ≤ H ∧ Function.Surjective (actualMatrix d H).mulVecLin

def AnalyticAggregateStatement : Prop :=
  ∀ nu : ℝ, 2 < nu → ∀ d : FixedData nu,
    ∃ error : ℝ → ℝ, Tendsto error atTop (𝓝 0) ∧
      ∀ᶠ H : ℝ in atTop, ∀ selection : Row d H → Column d H,
        (actualMinor d H selection).det ≠ 0 →
        Real.log ‖(actualMinor d H selection).det‖ / ((actualRowCount d H : ℝ) * H) ≤
          d.analyticError + error H +
            max (-collisionRate d H)
              (-nu * ((d.base.A : ℝ) * (1 - d.base.eta) - actualMean d H))

end OAI.PiExponent.DeterminantContradiction

publish_jobs.theorem_title: Arithmetic data associated with interpolation minors
publish_jobs.natural_language_statement:
Let $p_i\in\mathbb Z$ and $q_i\in\mathbb N$ be numerators and denominators. For real parameters $F,v_0,H$ and a natural row multiplicity $K$, define

$$w_i=\lceil\log q_i\rceil_+,\qquad r_i=\frac{2\mathrm i p_i}{q_i},\qquad T_i=\left\lceil\frac{F w_i}{v_0}\right\rceil_+.$$

Here the ceiling symbols denote natural ceilings. The weighted row sum is the sum of $\sum_i b_iw_i$ over the exact source row domain. Its normalized mean divides this sum by the row count times $H$. For any selection of columns indexed by the rows, the selected minor is the resulting square submatrix of the logarithmic interpolation matrix. These quantities are the data used in the later determinant estimates.

namespace OAI.PiExponent.MatrixArithmetic

open scoped BigOperators

noncomputable def logWeights {m : ℕ} (q : Fin m → ℕ) (i : Fin m) : ℝ :=
  (⌈Real.log (q i)⌉₊ : ℝ)

noncomputable def rationalCenters {m : ℕ} (p : Fin m → ℤ) (q : Fin m → ℕ) : Fin m → ℂ :=
  fun i => 2 * Complex.I * (p i : ℂ) / (q i : ℂ)

noncomputable def truncationOrders {m : ℕ} (q : Fin m → ℕ) (F v0 : ℝ) : Fin m → ℕ :=
  fun i => ⌈F * logWeights q i / v0⌉₊

noncomputable def rowWeightedSum {m : ℕ} (K : ℕ) (v0 θ : ℝ)
    (q : Fin m → ℕ) (H : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ ρ : InterpolationMatrix.Row K v0 θ (logWeights q) H,
    ∑ i, (ρ.2.1 i.succ : ℝ) * logWeights q i

noncomputable def meanRowWeight {m : ℕ} (K : ℕ) (v0 θ : ℝ)
    (q : Fin m → ℕ) (H : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  rowWeightedSum K v0 θ q H /
    ((Fintype.card (InterpolationMatrix.Row K v0 θ (logWeights q) H) : ℝ) * H)

noncomputable def selectedMinor {m : ℕ} (K : ℕ) (w0 v0 θ F H : ℝ)
    (p : Fin m → ℤ) (q : Fin m → ℕ)
    (selection : InterpolationMatrix.Row K v0 θ (logWeights q) H →
      InterpolationMatrix.Column w0 (logWeights q) H) :
    Matrix (InterpolationMatrix.Row K v0 θ (logWeights q) H)
      (InterpolationMatrix.Row K v0 θ (logWeights q) H) ℂ :=
  (InterpolationMatrix.truncatedLogMatrix K w0 v0 θ (logWeights q) H
    (rationalCenters p q) (truncationOrders q F v0)).submatrix id selection

end OAI.PiExponent.MatrixArithmetic

publish_jobs.theorem_title: Core polynomial data for interpolation matrices
publish_jobs.natural_language_statement:
For natural exponent vectors $a,b$ indexed by $m$ coordinates, complex centers $r_i$, polynomials $G_i$, and natural numbers $j,h,s$, define the monomial image and its coefficient entry by

$$M_{j,h,a}= (1+X)^h\prod_i(jr_i+G_i+Y_i)^{a_i},\qquad A_{(j,s,b),(h,a)}=[X^sY^b]M_{j,h,a}.$$

The finite exponent vector is the finitely supported form of $a$. The truncated logarithm of order $T$ is the polynomial truncation of the formal series $\log(1+X)$. The interpolation matrix uses these entries on the exact weighted row and column domains; its logarithmic specialization sets $G_i$ equal to the corresponding truncated logarithm. These definitions supply the matrix data of the conditional determinant argument.

import Mathlib.Algebra.MvPolynomial.Eval
import Mathlib.Algebra.Order.Antidiag.FinsuppEquiv
import Mathlib.Analysis.Asymptotics.SpecificAsymptotics
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Log.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Pow.Real
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Trigonometric.Bounds
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecificLimits.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecificLimits.Normed

import Mathlib.Tactic

import Definitions.Def_OAI_NumberTheory_PiExponent_Polynomials_SimplexCounting_WeightedDomains

namespace OAI.PiExponent.InterpolationMatrix

open scoped BigOperators

noncomputable def exponentVector {m : ℕ} (a : Fin m → ℕ) : Fin m →₀ ℕ :=
  Finsupp.equivFunOnFinite.symm a

noncomputable def truncatedLog (T : ℕ) : Polynomial ℂ :=
  PowerSeries.trunc T (PowerSeries.log ℂ)

noncomputable def monomialImage {m : ℕ} (r : Fin m → ℂ)
    (G : Fin m → Polynomial ℂ) (j h : ℕ) (a : Fin m → ℕ) :
    MvPolynomial (Fin m) (Polynomial ℂ) :=
  MvPolynomial.C ((1 + Polynomial.X) ^ h) *
    ∏ i, (MvPolynomial.C (Polynomial.C ((j : ℂ) * r i) + G i) +
      MvPolynomial.X i) ^ a i

noncomputable def entry {m : ℕ} (r : Fin m → ℂ)
    (G : Fin m → Polynomial ℂ) (j s : ℕ) (b : Fin m → ℕ)
    (h : ℕ) (a : Fin m → ℕ) : ℂ :=
  ((monomialImage r G j h a).coeff (exponentVector b)).coeff s

noncomputable def matrix {m : ℕ} (K : ℕ) (w0 v0 θ : ℝ)
    (w : Fin m → ℝ) (H : ℝ) (r : Fin m → ℂ) (G : Fin m → Polynomial ℂ) :
    Matrix (Row K v0 θ w H) (Column w0 w H) ℂ :=
  fun ρ c => entry r G ρ.1.val (ρ.2.1 0) (fun i => ρ.2.1 i.succ)
    (c.1 0) (fun i => c.1 i.succ)

noncomputable def truncatedLogMatrix {m : ℕ} (K : ℕ) (w0 v0 θ : ℝ)
    (w : Fin m → ℝ) (H : ℝ) (r : Fin m → ℂ) (T : Fin m → ℕ) :
    Matrix (Row K v0 θ w H) (Column w0 w H) ℂ :=
  matrix K w0 v0 θ w H r (fun i => truncatedLog (T i))

end OAI.PiExponent.InterpolationMatrix
